mechanism_fidelity.rationale: Handoff delays affect travel times across overlapping routes. Comparing measured times with model predictions and iteratively fitting structured residuals preserves the source's inverse-model chain. Coverage, clock error, workload variation and non-uniqueness retain relevant limits on reconstruction.

target_fidelity.rationale: Constraining possible handoff-delay fields directly contributes to identifying which handoffs account for end-to-end delay. The inference explicitly stops short of a unique causal explanation.

operational_coherence.rationale: Known routes, synchronized timing across overlapping paths and an additive-delay model checked under controlled conditions support fitting handoff delays from route-time residuals. The resulting inference is appropriately bounded to possible delay fields.

validity.rationale: All three criteria pass: the mapping preserves model-based inference from overlapping paths, addresses the retained handoff-delay question and has an established target measurement basis for its bounded conclusion.

uncertainty: The packet does not establish how precisely individual handoff delays can be distinguished; coverage and non-uniqueness limit resolution.
The model's reliability beyond the controlled operating conditions is unspecified.
